title: Progressive Invocation Gradient: SDK heuristics & streaming-tool contract
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a working PRD-style playbook for a progressive invocation model we want to expose in Hosted API SDKs: a first-class, ergonomic surface for partially-materialized streaming responses that can invoke tools, yield typed frames, and gracefully degrade/resume. The goal is to provide clear heuristics for SDK ergonomics, an RPC/stream contract for tool-calls + structured output, and an acceptance checklist for engineering+SDK teams.

Context / problem we keep seeing:
- Customers need lower-latency partial responses (progressive answers) while the model continues generation.
- Tooling requires the ability to call external actions mid-stream (search, DB lookup, code execution) with minimal fragility and good developer ergonomics.
- Current SDK patterns either force users to choose between raw streaming (text chunks) and heavyweight structured tool orchestration. We want a middle ground: typed frames + action lifecycle hooks + resume semantics.

High-level proposal (core ideas):
1) Progressive Invocation Gradient (PIG) surface: SDK method that returns a typed async iterator of "frames". Frames are small, composable units that may be: text_fragment, structured_object, action_request, action_response, checkpoint, resume_token, or heartbeat. Each frame includes a minimal header with indexing and optional schema id.

2) Action lifecycle model: action_request frames declare a tool invocation with an idempotency key and schema. The SDK exposes: onActionRequest (developer can intercept, run tool, and post action_response) or configure automatic tool-router bindings. Action responses can be partial (streamed) as well.

3) Structured-first default with flexible parsing: SDKs should offer a structured parse helper that attempts to assemble coherent JSON/typed output from frames, but fall back to raw token stream when partial/invalid JSON arrives. Provide a tolerant parser that returns (partial_object, validation_errors, source_frames).

4) Backpressure & priority hints: frames can carry priority_hint and estimated_cost to help client SDKs or intermediate proxies decide buffering, eager parasitic tool runs, or user-visible progressive snippets.

API sketch (Node-style pseudo):
// simplified
const stream = client.invokeProgressive({
  model: 'rwx-4b',
  prompt: prompt,
  toolBindings: {search: localSearchShim},
  parseSchema: 'doc-summary-v1'
});
for await (const frame of stream) {
  switch(frame.type) {
    case 'text_fragment': display(frame.text); break;
    case 'action_request': // SDK helper optionally auto-handles
      if (!frame.handled) runTool(frame).then(r => client.postActionResponse(frame.id, r));
      break;
    case 'structured_object': tryApply(frame.payload); break;
    case 'checkpoint': saveResume(frame.token); break;
  }
}

Frame-level contract (wire semantics):
- All frames are newline-delimited JSON objects over the stream socket (or frames with length prefix in HTTP/2 multiplex).
- Minimal fields: {frame_id, seq, type, schema_id?, ts, payload?} where payload is opaque string or JSON depending on type.
- action_request must include: {action_id, tool_name, idempotency_key, inputs_schema_id, estimated_wait_ms?}.
- action_response: {action_id, status: ok|err|partial, payload, resume_token?}.

Resume & idempotency
- Streams may emit checkpoint frames that contain short resume tokens that map to the server-side request state. SDKs persist tokens and re-open streams specifying token to resume from a checkpoint.
- Tool action idempotency uses idempotency_key and action_id so on retries servers and SDKs can avoid duplicate runs or reconcile partial responses.

SDK ergonomics principles (opinionated):
- Default to structured-first: client helpers should attempt to present fully-assembled structured output (object API) but expose raw frame stream for advanced use.
- Keep the simple case tiny: a one-liner helper (client.progressiveSummary(prompt)) that returns the final draft object or raises an well-described ValidationError with partials.
- Tool call as async hooks: use a single onActionRequest callback in the SDK constructor so users can wire tool connectors centrally rather than per-call.
- Backpressure awareness: SDKs must expose a per-frame consumer.pause()/resume() primitive and a high-water mark config. Default high-water mark tuned for mobile (32KB) and server (1 MB).
- Portable error model: frames with type 'error' include an error_class, retriable boolean, and suggested_client_action (retry|skip|fallback).

Migration and rollout plan (staged):
- Alpha: internal SDKs only, limited tests with dev-power customers who need incremental outputs for search assistants.
- Beta: opt-in flag in hosted API (progressive_invocation=true). Collect telemetry on frame rates, action latency, client restarts.
- GA: default SDK helpers and full docs, deprecate earlier ad-hoc partial-output surfaces.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SDKs (Node & Python) can consume frame streams and reconstruct structured_object for at least 90% of our internal prompt suite without manual patches.
- Action lifecycle works end-to-end for bound local tools (search) with <150ms median additional latency for action round-trips in the same region.
- Resume tokens successfully resume in >=95% of simulated intermittent-network cases in SRE harness.
- Telemetry surfaces per-frame metrics: frames/sec, action_request_rate, action_error_rate, resume_attempts.

Observability / telemetry notes:
- Tag frames with request_id and session_id. Track time delta between action_request emitted and action_response received (for SLA breakpoints).
- Provide dev-mode logs that surface partial-parse failures in readable format (frame seq, raw payload, parser error).

Edge cases and heuristics (working list):
- When partial structured payload looks like truncated JSON, do not block finalizing text fragments; present best-effort merged object and attach validation_errors.
- If action_request declares estimated_wait_ms >> latency SLO, SDK should surface a warning and optionally ask app to run action asynchronously (return a placeholder and continue).
- Long-lived sessions: introduce a periodic checkpoint every N frames or M seconds to reduce resume window.

Open questions (needs design/eng):
- Should frames be pure JSON objects or binary-level length prefixed for HTTP/2 gRPC performance? (perf team to benchmark).
- How to present security boundaries for automatic tool bindings in dedicated/private deployments (explicit allowlist vs. capability-scoped tokens)?
- Best default high-water mark across mobile, web, server footprints — propose: mobile 32KB, web 128KB, server 1MB. Confirm with SDK team.

Implementation notes / TODOs:
- [ ] Wire basic frame schema into hosted-api server; produce sample streams for SDK tests (PRO-2021).
- [ ] Implement Node/Python client frame iterator with pause/resume and built-in tolerant parser. (owner: Tomás)
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks in Console (per-frame breakdown and action latency heatmap) (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Draft public examples and migration guide for existing streaming users.

Related references and prior work:
- Previously discussed incremental-tool-emulator-spec-wip (see linked artifacts).
- streaming-handshake-compact-frames-and-sdk-resume-prd-wip — we should reconcile framing choices.

Appendix: brief UX scenarios
1) Search-augmented assistant (mobile): user types query, app shows immediate 1-2 sentence progressive summary (text_fragment frames) while an action_request for search is emitted; when search results arrive, structured_object frames with citations arrive and the app updates the summary to include sources. Resume token allows app to reconnect after backgrounding.

2) Code synthesis with build check: model streams a patch as text fragments; once a test-run action_request is emitted, SDK runs a local build tool, posts action_response; model receives results and streams a final structured_object with diagnostic fields.

Style and docs guidance for examples:
- Keep code samples < 20 lines for quickstart.
- Provide a debugging guide that explains common parse failures and how to toggle strict vs tolerant parse modes.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally heuristic-first; asking for feedback on where to add more rigid wire-level type definitions vs keeping SDK-level flexibility.
- Please add any missing real-customer scenarios we should test against in the acceptance suite.

-- end --
